title: A 38m Hall Stands With Zero Nails — Pillars or the Echo Wall? | China Travel Expert
description:
Beijing's Temple of Heaven hides one of the great tricks of Chinese carpentry. The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests rises about 38 metres on a triple marble terrace, and its roof is held up entirely by interlocking wood joints — no iron nails and no cement at all.

Inside stand 28 wooden pillars, and each ring means something: the 4 central "dragon-well" columns stand for the seasons, the 12 around them for the months, and the outer 12 for the traditional Chinese double-hours of the day.

Walk a few minutes south and you reach the Echo Wall, a smooth circular wall that carries a whisper spoken at one side all the way round to the other.

★ Expert Tip: come right at opening, before the tour groups. The Echo Wall only works when it's quiet — stand close and speak softly ALONG the wall, not across the courtyard.
